instructions.text: Gather the elderberries when quite ripe; put them into a stone jar, mash them with a round stick, and set them in a warm oven, or in a large kettle of boiling water till the jar is hot through, and the berries begin to simmer
Then take them out, and press and strain them through a sieve
To every quart of juice allow a pound of Havanna or Lisbon sugar, and two quarts of cold soft water
Put the sugar into a large kettle, pour the juice over it, and, when it has dissolved, stir in the water
Set the kettle over the fire, and boil and skim it till the scum ceases to rise

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Gather the elderberries when quite ripe; put them into a stone jar, mash them with a round stick, and set them in a warm oven, or in a large kettle of boiling water till the jar is hot through, and the berries begin to simmer
2. Then take them out, and press and strain them through a sieve
3. To every quart of juice allow a pound of Havanna or Lisbon sugar, and two quarts of cold soft water
4. Put the sugar into a large kettle, pour the juice over it, and, when it has dissolved, stir in the water
5. Set the kettle over the fire, and boil and skim it till the scum ceases to rise
6. To four gallons of the liquor add a pint and a half of brandy
7. Put it into a keg, and let it stand
